verdicts.summary: Lean uses a different formula here. The expression is matched term for term — representativeFrequency B σ u L K g = B•(K − (σu/(L‖g‖²))•g) has the same B_s, the same σ, the same u_*, the same L_s and the same g₀ = shearVector F₀ G₀ q₀ = (R∂_R F, ∂_R G), and the two components are read off as the paper does (target = R₀·(frequency)₀ is p̃, (frequency)₁ is p_z) — but the vector K it is applied to is the opposite of the paper's. The repository's K is transverseDirection g = −quarterTurn(normalDirection g) = (N_z, −Nθ), while the paper's sentence 'We use the quarter turn K = (−N_z, Nθ)' makes K = quarterTurn N. Writing K_p for the paper's and c = σu_*/(L_s|g₀|²), the Lean vector is B_s(−K_p − c g₀) = −B_s(K_p − (−σ)u_*g₀/(L_s|g₀|²)), i.e. minus the paper's wave vector for the opposite sign σ. Both signs are constructed (PrimaryGeometryAssembly.family is indexed by c : Fin 2 with phaseSign c = ±1), and the repository's own frame relation quarterTurn K = N keeps every later formula consistent with its choice (FamilyData.eigen12/eigen21, PhaseEstimates.transverseDirection_close with n ≈ pack (B·s) (B•K)), so the two conventions produce the same unordered pair of phase gradients up to an overall sign. I verified that algebraic identity and the two definitions; I did not trace the downstream real wave field to confirm that the overall sign is absorbed there.
